minutes.summary: The Sewer Commission met remotely. A longtime member announced his resignation effective April 30 and a second member said he will step aside for several weeks. The main business was a motion to require permission rather than notification before members consult town counsel, which drew objections from the departing member and a resident. The commission also covered the Fitchburg agreement extension, maintenance plan review, the budget and minutes.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to change its town counsel policy from notification to permission before members consult counsel; the vote tally was not audible.
A longtime member announced his resignation effective April 30, and a second member said he will step aside for several weeks.
The business manager will check with the town clerk whether the vacancy is filled by appointment or put on the ballot.
A member will take over the Fitchburg agreement extension work, and a one-hour meeting of the maintenance plan reviewers is to be arranged.
The sewer budget has gone to the town manager and goes to the Finance Committee on March 11.

why_it_matters: The permission rule changes how commission members can get legal advice on sewer matters, which touch sewer bills, the Fitchburg treatment contract and the maintenance plan; a departing member and a resident objected that it limits members.
The vacancy may be filled by appointment or by a ballot vote, so residents may be asked to vote on a seat if the clerk confirms it goes to the ballot.
watch_next: Commission meeting March 9 at 5:00, then the Finance Committee budget presentation on March 11.
The town clerk's answer on whether the vacancy is appointed or goes on the ballot.
